title: Design MRU Queue
description:
Design a queue-like data structure `MRUQueue` that moves the most recently used element to the end of the queue:
- `MRUQueue(int n)` constructs the queue containing the `n` integers `[1, 2, 3, ..., n]` in order.
- `int fetch(int k)` moves the `k`-th element (**1-indexed**) to the end of the queue and returns its value.

Aim for `O(sqrt(n))` time per `fetch` using sqrt-decomposed linked-list buckets (or `O(log n)` with an order-statistic tree / Fenwick tree).
constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made to fetch.
hints: Partition the `n` elements into `ceil(n / B)` doubly linked lists (deques) of bucket size `B = isqrt(n) + 1`, so locating bucket `b = (k - 1) // B` and offset `(k - 1) % B` takes O(sqrt(n)) time.

After removing the fetched element from bucket `b` and appending it to the last bucket, shift the front element of bucket `j + 1` to the back of bucket `j` for each `j` from `b` to `numBuckets - 2` in O(1) per bucket, preserving fixed bucket sizes.

examples.explanation: With n=1, the single element 1 is always fetched and placed back at index 1.
